questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: That I was able to spend a semester in another country and experience a different culture as well as the possibility to study at another university and seeing the difference in academic structure

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was easy, there was a big orientation day were every piece of information I needed was provided. I had also been sent the same information before the orientation day so I was fully prepared

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I received some assistance with my subject enrollment and getting my student card

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: There were multiple dorm options as well as individual apartments

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: There was a food relief system were you once a week could pick up between 4 and 7 frozen meals that had been preprepared and only needed to be heated in the microwave

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about on campus housing? *
questions.answer: It's a bit more expensive than finding housing out in the city but overall it's not that big of a difference once you factor in public transport

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: In the application process you also provided a list of courses you would like to be assessed to eligible to register for, once you had received an answer on that it only took a couple off minutes on the university portal to register for the rest of them

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: During the orientation week before semester start there was plenty of help on campus as well as online if you needed any assistance

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the classes I wanted to register for

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Make sure you do the proper research on your classes before applying because several of them have prerequisites that you need to satisfy

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I had three third year bachelor courses and one masters

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Here it was more lectures with a few tutorials while at UCPH it's still centered around the lectures but we have exercise classes every week where you are able to work on the questions, so at UCPH you get to work on the questions at the university more instead of having to do all of them at home or in the few tutorials there are through the semester

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Theoretical Physics 3, 
Condensed Matter Physics, 
Sub-atomic Physics, 
General Relativity

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Theoretical Physics 3, Condensed Matter Physics and General Relativity are all excellent courses with good lecturers, though General Relativity is a pretty advanced and difficult course and you need to make sure you're ready for it before doing the course

Food DKK per month *

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: In general there weren't many unexpected costs for me, the only one I can think of is that the rent system is every 14 days meaning that one month I had to pay rent three times instead of two times that was the norm

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: In general food prices are mostly the same as in Denmark, however meat are actually a lot cheaper for the most part

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There were plenty of clubs you could join and during the orientation week you had the opportunity to meet them all and find those you would like to be a part of

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Definitely join the MUSEX club because they focus on making activities for exchange students like welcome parties and just in general giving you an opportunity to meet a lot of the other exchange students at the university

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Definitely explore the different suburbs of the city, because they are all so unique and different. But also doing day trips or even renting a car for weekend and exploring more of the country side like Phillip Island or taking a trip down the Great Ocean Road. Also doing some weekend or week trips to Sydney, Tasmania or some of the other big cities is definitely a recomendation

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy, the cultural difference is not that big from Denmark

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Just start getting to know those you have classes with and slowly you will meet more local students. Or you could join a club and meet them there

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I didn't find anything that challenging

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Definitely the openness and kindness that they show towards everyone. Almost every person you talk to wants to get to know more about you and just in general they are really nice to have social gatherings with

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Do your course research in good time, because the handbook isn't the easiest thing to navigate
Join a club, because it gives you the opportunity to meet a lot of other students than just those you have classes with
Definitely explore the city and country on your weekends and in your holiday, because it's such a different and amazing place with so much to see and do

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Knowing that there is a food relief program is a good thing to know, because it provides you with several free meals and frees up some money you can spend elsewhere on your exchange

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Definitely once the exams were over and knowing I had completed the academic part of my exchange and then be able to see as much as could of Australia before going back to Denmark

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Definitely getting used to having classes only in English meaning that I had to start thinking in English in order to keep up, also the examination system is so different because nearly all exams are without books or any other assistance, meaning you had to remember all of the syllabus yourself and could not just look it up in the book

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
